def: The information content of an event, -log p, which is large for rare events and adds across independent ones.
The unit of information when logarithms are base 2: the surprise of a fair coin landing heads, or one yes/no question.
The unit of information when logarithms are natural; one nat is about 1.4427 bits.
The expected surprise of a distribution, which is also the least average number of bits per symbol a lossless code can use.
The average surprise of a model q over data drawn from p, H(p, q); a training loss is a sample estimate of it.
The extra bits paid per symbol for using q instead of the true p, KL(p || q) = H(p, q) - H(p); non-negative, asymmetric and not a distance.
KL(p || q) punishes a model for missing mass the truth has and so covers all modes; KL(q || p) punishes mass the truth lacks and so locks onto one mode.
Two raised to the cross-entropy in bits: the effective number of equally likely choices per token.
A model's total cross-entropy on a text divided by the text's size in bytes, which compares models regardless of their tokenisers.
An optimal prefix code that gives short codewords to likely symbols, with average length within one bit of the entropy.
A term beta times KL(policy || reference) subtracted from the reward in RLHF-style training to keep the tuned model near its starting point.
The sample estimate (r - 1) - ln r of KL, with r the ratio of reference to policy probability, which is unbiased, non-negative and low in variance.
The KL divergence from a joint distribution to the product of its marginals: the bits of uncertainty about one variable removed by learning the other.
